species.habitat_description: Forests with grassy openings; uses large ranges while seeking plants and water.
species.geographic_description: Fragmented across 13 countries in South and Southeast Asia, from India to Borneo.
species.shape_description: Massive robust body with a trunk; many males have tusks.
species.diet_flora: Grasses, leaves, roots, vines, twigs, shoots, bark, and fruit.
species.behavior_1: Related females and young form cooperative herds; mature males are more solitary.
species.behavior_2: Grazes and browses and communicates over kilometres with low-frequency calls.
species.life_description_1: Matures at about 8-13 years; gestation lasts 21.5-22 months and usually produces one precocial calf.
species.key_fact_3: Protecting its wide range benefits many other species.
species.threats: Habitat fragmentation and loss, agriculture-related conflict, infrastructure, and poaching.

profile.habitat_note: Asian forests with grassy openings across large plant- and water-seeking ranges.
profile.morphology_note: Massive robust elephant with a trunk and tusks in many males.
profile.diet_note: Herbivore eating grasses, woody browse, bark, roots, and fruit.
profile.behavior_note: Cooperative female-led herds graze, browse, and communicate with low-frequency calls.
profile.reproduction_note: Usually one precocial calf follows a gestation of nearly 22 months.
profile.reference_summary: Endangered wide-ranging Asian herbivore threatened by habitat loss, conflict, infrastructure, and poaching.
